name: Louisiana

law.summary: Permittees report overflows and unauthorized discharges to LDEQ (24 hours; written report within 7 days) and emergencies to the State Police hotline. No duty to tell the public was found in statute, rule or the standard LPDES conditions; New Orleans and Baton Rouge consent decrees contain overflow response plans whose notice terms were not read.

citations.title: Notification of unauthorized discharges (emergency, non-emergency, written report)
citations.quote: The transmittal envelope and report or email subject line and report should be clearly marked "UNAUTHORIZED DISCHARGE NOTIFICATION REPORT." (per search snippet; written report within seven calendar days)
citations.channel: LDEQ SPOC / Louisiana State Police hotline
citations.threshold: above reportable quantity or emergency conditions

regulator_report.deadline: 24 hours oral (LPDES standard conditions, mirroring 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6)); 7 days written for unauthorized discharges

cso_permit_notice_clause.quote: No municipal CSO permits; the two EPA-inventory CSO permits are industrial plants.

bills_and_cases: U.S. v. Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans (E.D. La. 93-3212): 1998 decree, Third Modified Consent Decree 2014.
U.S. and Louisiana v. City of Baton Rouge / Parish of East Baton Rouge: 2002 decree, modified 2012-2013.
Bills of 2025-2026 on overflow notice: none found (search only).

erule.notes: No Louisiana rows in SOBE; LDEQ takes reports by phone, its online incident form and NetDMR noncompliance forms.

statewide_feed.notes: Reports may be retrievable one PDF at a time from EDMS; untested.

cso.notification_practice: No municipal CSOs. The seed's 2 permits / 2 outfalls are industrial plants (Shell Geismar, LACC Westlake).

sso.notes: No public SSO location source found.

beaches.program: LDH Beach Monitoring Program (23 coastal sites; weekly Thursday advisories May to October)
beaches.notes: LDH site returned 403 (bot protection) to this machine.

habs.program: LDH ad hoc algal bloom advisories
habs.notes: No standing program page or list.

health_department_pages: LDH news releases (beach and algal bloom advisories)
LDH general 'swim at your own risk' advisory for all public waterways (per search)

barriers.what: No public-notice duty; overflow reports go only to LDEQ and the State Police.
Overflow reports, if kept, are reachable only one document at a time in EDMS or by public records request.
LDH beach monitoring pages return 403 to automated fetches.
barriers.note: Ask LDH for a data feed or use Swim Guide / BEACON.

readiness.rationale: No statewide overflow list, no SOBE rows and no municipal CSOs; only EDMS documents (untested) and consent-decree reports. Louisiana shows plant outfalls, the rain caution and the plain statement, plus LDH beach advisories once the 403 is solved.

owner_questions: Label the two industrial 'CSO' permits as industrial combined outfalls, or drop them from the sewage CSO count?
Ask LDH for beach advisory data access (their site blocks automated fetches)?
Worth a records request to LDEQ for SSO reports, to make the barrier visible?
surprise: Louisiana's only two 'CSO' permits in EPA's inventory are petrochemical plants (Shell Geismar and an ethylene plant at Westlake), not sewer systems; the state has no municipal CSOs and no public overflow reports at all.
